observation.body:
## Problem

The issue #39 / PR #41 harness run required agents to coordinate individual verification commands, wait for command-intent acknowledgements, launch bounded groups through temporary scripts, collect logs, check coverage and manually assemble evidence reports. Most of that work is deterministic. Repeating it for the implementer and independent checkers increases latency and opportunities for transcription or coverage errors.

The repository already has CMake presets/CTest for Fossilize and a Python unittest-based harness runner with discovery, bounded groups and exact-union verification. Reuse those facilities. Today the planner chooses checks; there is no general automatic changed-file test selector. Running a task through the harness must not by itself require testing the harness implementation.

## Required outcome

Provide one supported repository-owned verification entry point that executes the approved, change-scoped verification manifest and produces complete machine-readable execution evidence. The same project runner adapters should be reusable locally and in CI; harness execution adds its existing intent, identity and publication requirements. Standalone test results do not grant harness acceptance.

The planner still designs appropriate checks. Fresh implementers and independent checkers still execute their own required checks, inspect assertions and judge correctness. Automate execution and evidence collection while preserving these roles and acceptance gates.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **One command for a complete selected verification run.** The command resolves and validates the intended manifest, runs its required checks with real deadlines and bounded concurrency, collects logs/results, verifies complete coverage and emits a compact outcome plus evidence references. Record the approved command bundle through the canonical writer before execution so routine checks do not require agent-to-agent acknowledgement for each command. Preserve lock/CAS, stale-worker fencing, role permissions, budget limits and exact artifact-publication guarantees. Workers do not gain arbitrary canonical-state mutation authority. No temporary launcher/report-building scripts or manually typed per-command evidence are needed in the normal supported workflow.

2. **Verification remains scoped to the change and requirements.** The resolved manifest explicitly identifies selected suites/profiles, prerequisites, exclusions and the rationale/criterion coverage. Ordinary Fossilize C++ changes select the relevant build/CTest checks; the Python harness suite is not added merely because the harness is managing the task. Harness-only changes run the required harness checks without configuring/building C++, invoking GPU tests or launching Steam by default. Mixed changes include both relevant sets. Shared build configuration, guidance or cross-component changes require an explicit impact assessment. File paths may inform selection but cannot silently override required acceptance or prove unrelatedness. An ambiguous or incomplete selection must be exposed for review; it cannot silently omit required checks. The command executes the approved manifest and does not redesign acceptance independently.

3. **Reuse existing project runners.** Use existing CMake/CTest registrations and presets for native checks, and extend/reuse the existing Python harness runner for harness checks. Preserve full unittest discovery, bounded groups, scenario ownership and exact-union validation for the selected harness suite. Consume structured provider results where supported, including CTest discovery/results, with explicit handling for empty discovery, skipped tests and provider errors. Builds, package checks and assertion-bearing tests remain distinct evidence. Do not require a new general test framework or a C++ toolchain to run Python-only harness checks.

4. **Keep harness-specific implementation in the harness hierarchy.** Put the bulk of the orchestration, runner adapters, verification profiles/manifests, schemas, evidence normalization, harness bookkeeping integration, tests and detailed harness documentation under `.agents/skills/implement-change-harness/` and its subdirectories, or an explicitly established successor harness root. A small entry-point/router script outside that hierarchy is permitted; keep it limited to argument handling/delegation and avoid duplicated harness policy there. Existing native tests and CMake/CTest definitions remain with the project components they serve. General documentation may link to detailed harness instructions; avoid spreading substantial harness logic/configuration throughout the root, `cli/`, native `test/` or unrelated `local-docs/` files. The CLI spelling and optional router location are implementation choices, not additional root-level deliverables.

5. **Evidence is generated from actual execution and bound to actual source.** Bind harness evidence to repository/root/run/role/attempt, approved plan/manifest, candidate/base and execution environment. Formal verification uses an isolated fixed candidate with explicit source-identity/cleanliness checks; HEAD alone cannot conceal modified test source. Record actual commands, start/end/duration, exit status, discovered/selected/executed test and scenario identities, logs and limitations. Build mechanical report fields automatically from these records; leave semantic review, findings and verdict to the responsible agent. Missing, stale, duplicated, unfinished, failed, skipped or unexecuted mandatory results cannot satisfy acceptance. Keep normal output compact and reference immutable evidence rather than dumping unchanged history or embedding raw logs repeatedly in canonical state.

6. **Honest failure and restart behavior.** Failed, unavailable/unsupported, cancelled, timed-out and incomplete work remain distinct from success. Do not launch further queued expensive groups for a known-failing candidate merely to finish a success-shaped report; preserve completed failure facts and mark the remainder unexecuted/incomplete. Interrupted execution and uncertain evidence publication retain a precise supported resumption action. A restart cannot mix attempts/candidates, overwrite earlier results, discard failure evidence or fabricate a complete pass. Reuse isolation, process-lifetime and resource contracts already supported; this issue does not claim new unattended multi-run scheduling or authorize production GitHub, GPU or Steam effects.

7. **Supported workflow and documentation.** Update the harness skill/role/state guidance inside the harness hierarchy and add only concise project-level routing references where useful. Document the one-command invocation, scoped selection, native versus Python prerequisites, results, deadlines and recovery. An implementer, unit checker and separate final checker can each use it on their exact candidate without recurring per-test coordination. Preserve independent checking and explicit merge approval; this issue does not reduce checker passes or permit reuse of another role's execution as independent evidence.

## Required verification

Add assertion-bearing tests under the harness hierarchy, using disposable repositories, deterministic provider fixtures and bounded processes:

- Selection matrix: ordinary C++ change calls only its approved native checks; harness-only change calls only Python/harness checks and works without CMake/compiler availability; mixed/shared/ambiguous changes retain their declared requirements and review behavior. Assert actual adapter calls and absence of unrelated builds/GPU/Steam work.
- Runner reuse: native adapters invoke the intended existing presets/CTest commands and correctly interpret discovery/results; Python execution retains all required discovered IDs/scenarios and exact-union checks. Exercise zero tests, missing tools, provider failures, skips and incompatible results. Use real supported CMake/CTest and Python smoke fixtures where available; identify any unverified provider claims explicitly.
- Coverage and identity controls: deliberately omit/duplicate a result, alter the manifest, use a stale role/attempt/candidate, modify source, or supply failed/incomplete/skipped output; acceptance evidence must be rejected.
- Process/evidence failure matrix: nonzero child exit, real timeout/cancellation, interruption before/after result capture, restart, stale output paths and artifact publication failure. Assert bounded concurrency, owned scratch paths, retained failure facts and honest resumability without unrelated-file cleanup.
- Workflow control: one supported invocation executes a complete approved verification manifest and builds its mechanical evidence package without individual command-ack conversations, temporary launchers or manually assembled result envelopes. Tests remain scoped while independent role verdicts and publication fences remain unchanged.

Run the relevant existing harness regression suite. This filing is not evidence that the new command or selection policy exists or passes today.

## Scope, relationships and supporting evidence

Parent: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/9.

Builds on delivered https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/39 and https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/pull/41. The session audit observed five interrupted/timed-out aggregate-suite attempts before bounded execution was established, repeated command-intent handshakes and manual evidence assembly. The completed candidate nevertheless passed the implementer, fresh unit checker and separate final checker gates; preserve that rigor.

Existing implementation references: [native test registration](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/master/test/CMakeLists.txt), [CMake presets](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/master/CMakePresets.json), [Python harness runner](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/master/.agents/skills/implement-change-harness/scripts/run_harness_tests.py), and [verification guidance](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/master/local-docs/verification.md).

Related https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/40 owns safe concurrent runs, shared-resource enforcement and unattended scheduling. Integrate with its supported interfaces if delivered; do not duplicate that work or make it a prerequisite solely because both features launch checks. No blocked-by edge is asserted by this filing. State compaction/history-cache optimization, broader harness redesign and changes to Fossilize C++ behavior are separate work except for minimal integration required by this command.

This request authorizes filing the implementation issue, not starting its implementation or a new harness run.

observation.title: Add a change-scoped verification command using existing CMake/CTest and Python runners
